newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums weak, more mills in crushing.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums weak, more mills in crushing.

text.p: News that Iran was seeking to buy 170,000 tonnes of sugar has failed to buoy the Thai sugar market and premiums remained under pressure, trade sources said on Wednesday.
Thai sugar premiums were stable to lower this week as major buyers remained absent.
Premiums for raw sugar for January/March delivery were quoted around 0.70/0.90 cents (bid/offer) a pound over New York futures, unchanged from a week earlier.
March/May and May/July deliveries both dipped to 0.45/0.55 cents over New York from 0.50/60 cents and 0.55/0.60 cents last week.

Some traders expected Thailand to get a good portion of Iran's order if it does go ahead with the purchase. Iran is a major buyer of Thai sugar, importing more than 300,000 tonnes during the first 10 months of 1996.
"But there is nothing concrete on that yet. And the amount is not that big since we might have to share the cake with others," one Thai trader said.
Besides Thailand, other main sugar suppliers to Iran included Australia, Brazil and Cuba.
But traders see limited downside to Thai sugar premiums.
"The premiums (are) already too low. I don't think anyone would sell below this level," said another trader.
"But at the same time, the prices will continue to be pressured by news on surplus and a lack of major buyers such as China," he said.

More sugar mills in the northeast of the country have started crushing operations after a delay, while mills in the central region planned to speed up their crushing schedules, according to sources in the Sugar Board.
"I don't have a precise figure at the moment (on) how many mills have opened, but many have informed us of the operations last week," said an official at the board.
There are 46 sugar mills in Thailand. Mills in each region have different crushing schedules with northeastern mills normally the first to start.

At Thai ports, the sugar vessel movement was slow this week with only one new declaration. Yon Bong was scheduled to arrive on Wednesday to load 2,515 tonnes of white sugar for delivery to North Korea.
Thai sugar exports during the first 10 months of 1996 rose 17.8 percent year-on-year to 4.29 million tonnes, with Japan the biggest buyer so far.
